Summarise the alpha values of drawn pixels in a pain drawing

Source: R/pdr_summarize_rgba.R
pdr_summarize_rgba.Rd

Computes summary statistics of the alpha channel of the .rgba array of each drawing, using only pixels whose alpha falls within alpha_range (lower bound exclusive, upper bound inclusive). The number of drawn pixels (px) and the proportion of the canvas covered (area_prop) describe how much was drawn, while e.g. mean or median describe how dark or opaque the strokes are. Optionally, each drawing is first multiplied by one or more stencils (e.g. body regions) so that statistics are computed per region.

Usage

pdr_summarize_rgba(
  .data,
  pdr_col = pdr_data,
  summary_stat = "seven",
  alpha_range = c(0, 1),
  stencils = NULL
)

Arguments

.data

A pdr_tibble (see pdr_match()) whose pdr_drawings contain an .rgba element. Add it first with pdr_add_rgba().

pdr_col

<tidy-select> One or more list-columns of .data (pdr_lists) with .rgba in each drawing. Defaults to pdr_data. Unquoted names, strings and selections such as c(a, b) are accepted; each selected column is summarised separately.

summary_stat

Character vector of statistics to compute from the alpha values of the included pixels. Any of "px" (number of pixels), "area_prop" (px divided by .width * .height), "mean", "sd", "median", "iqr", "min", "max", "q1", "q5", "q10", "q25", "q75", "q90", "q95" and "q99" (the q statistics are quantiles at probabilities 0.01, 0.05, ..., 0.99). Two shortcuts are available when given as a single string: "seven" (default) is px, mean, max, min, median, sd and iqr; "all" is seven plus area_prop, q1, q5, q25, q75, q90, q95 and q99 (note: q10 is not included in "all", but can be requested explicitly). Columns are returned in a fixed order, not in the order requested: px, area_prop, mean, sd, median, iqr, min, max, q1, q5, q10, q25, q75, q90, q95, q99 (restricted to those requested). Note this differs from the order in which "seven" is listed above.

alpha_range

Numeric vector of length 2 giving the lower (exclusive) and upper (inclusive) alpha bounds of pixels to include, with 0 <= alpha_range[1] < alpha_range[2] <= 1. Defaults to c(0, 1), i.e. all drawn pixels. Use e.g. c(0.5, 1) to restrict to heavily drawn pixels.

stencils

Optional pdr_list in which each element has a .stencil (a height x width matrix of 0/1) and an .id, e.g. the list-column pdr_stencil_full_body$pdr_data or a list built with pdr_add_stencil(). Each stencil is applied (multiplied) to the alpha channel of every drawing before summarising, so the stencil dimensions must match the drawings. Defaults to NULL (no stencil). Note that this is deliberately plural and differs from stencil in pdr_modify_rgba().

Value

.data (a pdr_tibble) with added numeric columns, one per selected pdr_col and statistic (and per stencil, if stencils is given). Columns are named <pdr_col>_<stat> without stencils, and <pdr_col>_<stencil id>_<stat> with stencils, e.g. pdr_data_mean or pdr_data_Back_head_mean. If no pixels fall in alpha_range, px is 0, mean, sd, median, iqr and quantiles are NA, and min/max are Inf/-Inf (with a warning). If a drawing is missing (NA), its .rgba is NA, or its alpha channel is entirely NA, all statistics for that drawing, including px, are NA. Individual NA pixels are ignored.

Details

The drawings must already contain .rgba; see pdr_add_rgba(). For the terms pdr_drawing, pdr_list and pdr_tibble, see pdr_match().

See also

pdr_add_rgba() to add .rgba, pdr_add_stencil() and pdr_modify_rgba() for stencils, pdr_plot_rgba() to plot the arrays.

Examples

pd <- pdr_example_data |>
  dplyr::mutate(pdr_data = pdr_add_rgba(pdr_data))
#> `geom_path()`: Each group consists of only one observation.
#> ℹ Do you need to adjust the group aesthetic?

# Default: the "seven" statistics across all drawn pixels
pdr_summarize_rgba(pd)

# Selected statistics, only heavily drawn pixels

# Per stencil (here, two body regions)
pdr_summarize_rgba(
  pd,

)
